voyage.name: Freddys Bike Tours & Rentals
voyage.content: Bicycle hire and bike rentals. Also offers a range of guided bicycle tours through various Melbourne precincts.

voyage.name: Footscray Community Arts Centre
voyage.content: Non-stop art exhibitions and an endless list of music gigs and theatre shows. In summer outdoor film screenings take place on the banks of the Maribyrnong River.

voyage.name: Five Walls
voyage.content: Artist-run art space in the same place as Trocadero (above)

voyage.name: K Road Cliffs
voyage.content: An interesting cliff-face that overlooks the Werribee River, near the golf course. It's possible to launch canoes from the site along the river.

voyage.name: Moonee Ponds Courthouse Museum
voyage.address: Corner Mount Alexander Road and Kellaway Avenue, Moonee Ponds
voyage.content: The former Moonee Ponds Courthouse houses a museum of the local area, run by the Essendon Historical Society. In June 2016, a fire damaged the building and the collection, but it was restored.

voyage.name: Incinerator Gallery
voyage.content: Interesting gallery with exhibitions, art history talks, adult art courses, and workshops.

voyage.name: RAAF Museum
voyage.address: RAAF Base Williams, Point Cook Rd, Point Cook
voyage.content: The air-force base is still used for flying and training. Houses authentic aircraft in hangars, as well as numerous exhibitions and displays. Conducts free tours of the museum during weekdays. There are also options for pay joy-rides in old military aircraft.

voyage.name: Queens Park
voyage.address: Corner Mount Alexander Road and Kellaway Road, Moonee Ponds
voyage.content: A place to spend a relaxing day. There's a rose garden, a sunken garden, a lake, a cafe, and a 50-m pool open from November to March ($5.70 pool entry). Monuments include a cenotaph remembering Australia's dead in World War One, and a cairn marking the spot where the doomed Burke and Wills expedition camped on its first night heading out of Melbourne in 1860. There's a children's playground and an island rotunda, and

voyage.name: Werribee Mansion
voyage.price: Adult: $7, student/concession/child: $5, family (two adults and two children): $22
voyage.hours: Nov-Apr: daily 10AM-5:30PM; May-Oct: Mon-Fri 10AM-4PM, Sat Sun 10AM-5PM
voyage.content: An Italianate mansion from the 1870s, built by famous Scottish landlords Thomas and Andrew Chirnside. The building and its 60 rooms have been restored, and an audio tour is available. A café is available nearby. Paid tours depart Su-F at 11:30AM.

voyage.name: Werribee Historical Museum
voyage.address: Cnr Watton St & Duncans Rd, Werribee
voyage.content: Houses a collection of artefacts, documents, maps and photos relating to the Werribee area's history.

voyage.name: Werribee Park
voyage.content: A 10-acre park that used to be pastoral farmland. Includes fruit orchards, flower gardens, sculptures and wide open spaces. Contains many attractions, including Werribee Mansion and Zoo.

voyage.name: Victoria State Rose Garden
voyage.content: Winner of a global award for excellence, the gardens contain 5,000 roses in four interesting shapes. Roses look best from November to April.

voyage.name: Werribee Open Range Zoo
voyage.hours: Daily (including Christmas Day and all public holidays) 9AM-5PM, entry closes at 3:30PM. Sat Sun during Jan-Feb open till 9PM. Safari bus tours (50 minute) begin 10:30AM-3:40PM (Jan Feb: Sat Sun until 7:40PM)
voyage.content: An open range park with animals from the grasslands of Africa, Asia, North America and Australia.

voyage.name: Moonee Valley Racecourse
voyage.price: Most general admission tickets $20, GA for Cox Plate $55
voyage.hours: See website for race meeting dates and times
voyage.content: One of Melbourne's Big Three horse racing venues, there are several race meetings a month in the busy season from September to March. The famous Cox Plate weight-for-age race is run here in late October each year.

voyage.name: Moonee Ponds Clocktower Centre
voyage.content: Performing arts centre including drama, dance, music performances and movie screenings.

voyage.name: Altona Beach
voyage.content: On the "wrong" side of the bay in terms of famous Melbourne beaches, Altona Beach is a strictly locals-only affair. However, because it is a very long, clean, sandy beach, with plenty of parking, it is known as the best beach in Melbourne's west. Altona has a thriving restaurant and cafe district nearby, centred around Pier St. There's even a big new (2024) jetty, and the esplanade is lined with mature trees which pr

voyage.name: Footscray Market
voyage.hours: Tue Wed 7AM-4PM, Thu 7AM-6PM, Fri 7AM-7PM, Sat 7AM-5PM; closed Sun Mon
voyage.content: Footscray Market is a fresh produce, meat, poultry and seafood market, catering particularly to the various ethnicities and local restaurants. There's also eateries, nut and coffee stalls, tobacconists and a few variety shops. It has the reputation as one of the cheapest places in Melbourne to shop so if you're cooking for yourself it's definitely worth a look. Or just wander around and enjoy the sights and sounds of

voyage.name: Konjo African Craft
voyage.content: Store selling Ethiopian food and crafts: spices, flours, raw and roasted coffee, pots, wood craft, clothing and jewellery. Also has a cafe.

voyage.name: Pacific Werribee
voyage.content: A variety of specialty item stores including mens and ladies fashion, banks, beauty and food stores. Has over 150 stores including a 10-screen cinema.

voyage.name: Bharat Traders
voyage.content: A go-to shop for Indian ingredients, spices, food, homewares and other accoutrements.

voyage.name: Chestnut Tree Bookshop
voyage.content: A new bookshop and hangout space with all the trimmings, including coffee and vinyl.

voyage.name: Cafe Lalibela
voyage.content: Probably the best Ethiopian cuisine in the area, and not a main course over $12. Served in the traditional custom of sharing, the food is poured on layers of injera (flat, sour bread) covering one big plate to be shared by all at the table.

voyage.name: African Town Cafe
voyage.content: More Ethiopian cuisine, while local regulars pop in and out for a chat over excellent $2 Ethiopian coffee. All main courses $10.

voyage.name: Ras Dashen
voyage.content: A whole baked fish for $13, beans and egg in a mild stew for $8, nice dark "Amber Beer" from Ethiopia like a porter or mild stout.

voyage.name: Dumplings and More
voyage.content: Great entrees. The main courses not particularly cheap, but the entrees and dumplings are dirt cheap.

voyage.name: Konjo Cafe Footscray
voyage.content: Same location as Konjo African Craft in the "Buy" section above. Features a $15 all-you-can-eat buffet lunch W-Sa (vegan on W and Th).

voyage.name: Bar Thyme
voyage.content: Outstanding slightly fancy French fusion food with a romantic ambience. You'd never guess you were in Footscray.

voyage.name: Kariton Sorbetes
voyage.content: Filipino gelato with ever-changing, outlandish, delicious flavours. Once you try it, you'll wonder why they haven't taken over the world yet. They do take-away treats too. Worth waiting in line for.

voyage.name: Harley & Rose
voyage.content: WeFo's finest wood-fired pizza place. Unpretentious and delicious, good for families. Dining out front, inside and in courtyard.

voyage.name: Ollie's Deli
voyage.content: If you're ever in Footscray and feel like a gourmet sandwich that isn't a Banh Mi, this place is for you. They're so big you can easily share them, particularly the chicken schnitty and reuben sangers.

voyage.name: Cafe Sunshine
voyage.content: When the airport rail link is built through Sunshine, more tourists will have a reason to experience this suburb. This is a nice cafe with great coffee, food and service. It is particularly known for its Persian food. This cafe is also a social organisation which employs and trains people of refugee backgrounds.

voyage.name: Goje
voyage.price: Weigh-and-pay. Around $5 a serving if you don't go crazy - but it is hard not to!
voyage.content: Popular plant-based DIY frozen yoghurt place in the middle of the lively Yarraville restaurant and shopping strip. If coming by car, park a few streets away.

voyage.name: Laksa King
voyage.content: Supremely busy laksa place in the lively Newmarket shopping strip. Discount if paying by cash.

voyage.name: Latin Foods and Wines
voyage.content: Yes it is out in Melton, but if you're in the area, this is one of the best Latino restaurants in Melbourne. Expect the usual South American fare, plus regional specialties like Papusas and Arepas, all delicious.

voyage.name: The Station Hotel
voyage.content: Footscray - Opposite the Town Hall. Casual bar, indoor and outdoor seating, coffee. One of the "Top five places to eat steak" as judged by The Age Good Food Guide Dining Companion 2010.

voyage.name: Bar Josephine
voyage.content: Casual, cosy, tucked-away bar with interesting beers (including a beer lucky dip!) with board games and repurposed bus seats.

voyage.name: Mr West
voyage.content: Bar (upstairs) and bottle shop (downstairs) with a humongous number of beers on tap, plus wine and fancy spirits. Order pizza from the place across the street using QR codes at your table, or BYO food. Seating out front or upstairs. You can choose from the larger bottle shop selection and drink there as well.

voyage.name: The Victoria Hotel
voyage.content: Lovingly restored old pub with great food, dining areas inside, in courtyard, or outside.

voyage.name: Bonehead Brewing
voyage.content: On-site independent brewery with comfortable drinking area with open fireplace. There's usually food trucks out front.

voyage.name: West Footscray Wines
voyage.content: As WeFo gentrifies, outstanding little wine bars like this one are now possible. Get the staff to recommend you a bottle. Charcuterie and nibbles also available.

voyage.name: Hop Nation Brewing
voyage.hours: Thu 3-7PM, Fri 2-9PM, Sat noon-9PM, Sun noon-6PM
voyage.content: A hidden brewery worth making a trip for. Easily reached by the bike and pedestrian Maribyrnong River Trail. they also have outstanding pizza.

voyage.name: Plough Hotel
voyage.address: 333 Barkly Street (Corner Barkly St and Geelong Rd)
voyage.content: Above a large pub.

voyage.name: Mansion Hotel & Spa at Werribee Park
Moonee Ponds Courthouse Museum
voyage.address: Corner Mount Alexander Road and Kellaway Avenue, Moonee Ponds
voyage.content: The former Moonee Ponds Courthouse housed a museum of the local area, run by the Essendon Historical Society. In June 2016, a fire damaged the building and the collection. Restoration is happening, but the museum remains closed until further notice.

voyage.name: Incinerator Gallery
voyage.content: Interesting gallery with exhibitions, art history talks, adult art courses, and workshops.

voyage.name: Brunswick Town Hall and Counihan Gallery
voyage.hours: Library: Mon-Thu 10AM-8PM, Fri 10AM-6pm, Sat 9AM-4PM, Sun 1-5PM; gallery: Wed-Sat 11AM-5PM and Sun 1-5PM
voyage.address: Corner Sydney Road and Dawson Street, Brunswick
voyage.content: The historic Brunswick Town Hall contains the Brunswick Library branch of the Merri-bek City Council library, and the Counihan Gallery, a contemporary art space with changing exhibitions.

voyage.name: Street Art
voyage.address: Corner of Moreland Road and Holmes Street, Brunswick East
voyage.content: Melbourne is full of great street art and graffiti. Just one example is on the side of Worthy Apparel on Moreland Road as the number 8 tram turns left from Holmes Street. Go for a wander or ride the trams around and keep your eyes open for more great aerosol art.

voyage.name: Melbourne Olympic Village
voyage.content: The athletes village of the 1956 Melbourne Olympics resides in Heidelberg West, and has since been converted to public housing, a school, a small shopping centre amongst other uses. The original five-ring symbol of the Olympic Games still hangs over Alamein Rd as a testament to the area's history.

voyage.name: Queens Park
voyage.address: Corner Mount Alexander Road and Kellaway Road, Moonee Ponds
voyage.content: A place to spend a relaxing day. There's a rose garden, a sunken garden, a lake, a cafe, and a 50-m pool open from November to March ($5.70 pool entry). Monuments include a cenotaph remembering Australia's dead in World War One, and a cairn marking the spot where the doomed Burke and Wills expedition camped on its first night heading out of Melbourne in 1860. There's a children's playground and an island rotunda, and

voyage.name: CERES Community Environment Park
voyage.hours: Park open during daylight hours, check website for hours of different sections
voyage.address: Corner Roberts and Stewart Streets, Brunswick East
voyage.content: A place for community-based learning and action for environmental benefit, social justice, economic satisfaction, cultural enrichment and spiritual nurturing. Some of its facilities include an organic grocery open 9-5 every day with free live music on Wednesday, Saturday and Sunday mornings, a permaculture nursery and an organic cafe. There's a visitor centre and regular workshops, a nature play area and an energy pa

voyage.name: Loreto John York Park
voyage.content: If you've grabbed some cheap takeaway food and want to watch the trams sail by, or maybe if you have some children who need to let off some steam, this small park might be the perfect place. Named after the first Maltese-Australian to serve as Mayor of any Australian city, this park has a playground and an accessible water fountain.

voyage.name: Woodlands Historic Park
voyage.content: Immediately north of Melbourne Airport, contains an 1840s homestead and a nature reserve.

voyage.name: Moonee Valley Racecourse
voyage.price: Most general admission tickets $20, GA for Cox Plate $55
voyage.hours: See website for race meeting dates and times
voyage.content: One of Melbourne's Big Three horse racing venues, there are several race meetings a month in the busy season from September to March. The famous Cox Plate weight-for-age race is run here in late October each year

voyage.name: Moonee Ponds Clocktower Centre
voyage.content: Performing arts centre including drama, dance, music performances and movie screenings.

voyage.name: Brunswick Music Festival
voyage.content: Yearly music festival running for a week in March. It is kicked off with the Sydney Road Street Party where Sydney Road between Victoria Street and Brunswick Road is turned into a pedestrian zone with food stalls and outdoor stages at multiple locations.

voyage.name: Merri Creek Trail
voyage.content: Cycle or walk along Merri Creek. This is a 20km shared path free from motorized traffic between Yarra Bend Park, where the creek joins the Birrarung/Yarra River and the Main Yarra Trail in the south, and the Metropolitan Ring Road in the north.

voyage.name: Artocracy
voyage.content: Locally made fashion, food and gifts from a variety of artists.

voyage.name: Denimsmith
voyage.content: Jeans handmade in Brunswick East.

voyage.name: Infinity Jeans Outlet Store
voyage.address: Factory 8, 215 Nicholson Street, Brunswick East (access via Herbert Street)
voyage.content: Jeans made in Brunswick East.

voyage.name: Dejour Jeans
voyage.content: Local jeans business established in 1989. Until 2022 jeans were produced in Brunswick East. Free on-site alterations.

voyage.name: RetroStar Vintage warehouse
voyage.content: RetroStar Vintage has a warehouse sale about once a month, where every item is $10. Follow the News page on their website, or their Facebook page, for details of upcoming sales.

voyage.name: Cafe 2000
voyage.price: $11 big breakfast including coffee, $7 burgers, $4.50 thickshakes
voyage.content: There's nothing particularly amazing about the standard cafe meals here, but the prices are incredibly low. Right next to the tram and bus interchange, so definitely worth a look if you're in the area.

voyage.name: Mister Nice Guys Bakeshop
voyage.price: $11 dogs, baguettes and rolls, doughnuts, etc. $5.50, non-dairy cheesecake $8
voyage.content: Vegan, egg-free, dairy-free bakery with gluten-free (and many more) options. Five choices of non-dairy milks for coffee and shakes.

voyage.name: A1 Bakery
voyage.content: A Sydney Road classic, this place offers all sorts of Lebanese bakery products with pizzas for as little as $2. Cheese pies with halloumi, spinach and feta triangles, felafel or kafta wraps, platters from $6 - $12.

voyage.name: Rumi
voyage.content: Seriously great Middle Eastern food. Menu changes frequently so difficult to recommend specific dishes.

voyage.name: Cornish Arms
voyage.hours: Sat Sun kitchen open noon-9:30PM, Mon-Fri lunch 12-3, snacks and pizza 3-5:30PM, dinner 5:30-9:30PM
voyage.content: Pub with vegan-friendly tap beers and a vegan restaurant. Has a rooftop bar with views of the CBD.

voyage.name: The Green Refectory
voyage.content: Easy to miss, but better you don't, The Green Refectory serves great value homemade food, and quality Illy coffee to accompany it. I'm a fan of the gourmet salads, especially the tangy couscous salad with pumpkin, snow peas and heaps of mint, and eye off the homemade muffins, famous for their large and irregularly shape, for later. The crowd is eclectic mix of the Brunswick artsy crowd, university students and young

voyage.name: Sugardough
voyage.content: Quaint and lovely cafe. Another place that does a great breakfast. Egg and bacon panini or breakfast pie to start the day off, pies, panini and tarts for lunch and dinner. Cakes for dessert and a range of specialty bread to eat at home, including an olive sourdough loaf, and spelt bread.

voyage.name: Tiba's Restaurant
voyage.content: Tiba's Quality Lebanese food at very cheap prices. You can order a Shwarma plate for $14.80, and you will get rice, salad, bread, dips and meat. Again, this restaurant has large servings. They also have very nice Baklava and do great coffee. The front end of the restaurant is for take-aways, as they also do kebabs. The restaurant is 100% halal and alcohol free, however you can do take away on the food if you really n

voyage.name: Ovens Street Bakery
voyage.content: Great local bakery. Also makes delicious pizza slices. Only has outdoor seating.

voyage.name: Half Moon Cafe
voyage.content: Has a selection of Egyptian style falafel wraps. Taste is first class. Very on trend for the Coburg locals.

voyage.name: The Alderman
voyage.content: Low key, comfortable and cosy bar. Just like Fitzroy bars used to be like. Small courtyard in the back. Sicilian food from Bar Idda (next door) can be ordered.

voyage.name: The Brunswick Green
voyage.price: Most wine $8.50 a glass, chips $8 a bowl
voyage.content: The best beer garden in Brunswick (and possibly Melbourne), with live music outside on Sunday afternoon. The best place to spend a summers afternoon.

voyage.name: My Aeon
voyage.content: Techno/psy-trance club offering two floors, large smokers' area and fantastic Funktion-One speakers. Different events every night.

voyage.name: Gales Brewery
voyage.content: Small local neighbourhood brewery, with the two brewers recommending and serving their beers. You can bring your own food.

voyage.name: Alchemy Brewing
voyage.content: In addition to their craft beer, they also have great food.

voyage.name: Temple Brewing Co
voyage.content: Certified independent brewery. The menu features South American food.

voyage.name: Bridge Road Brewers
voyage.content: In 2024, the brewery from Beechworth, Victoria established their branch in Melbourne. Certified independent brewery.

voyage.name: The Foreigner Brewing Company
voyage.content: Small brewery in an industrial area with Czech-style beers.

voyage.name: Inner North Brewing Co
voyage.content: Certified independent brewery.

voyage.name: CoConspirators Brewing Co
voyage.content: Certified independent brewery.

voyage.name: Australian Jazz Museum
voyage.content: Dedicated to preserving Australia’s jazz heritage, this museum houses an extensive collection of jazz memorabilia, from instruments to historical recordings. It’s a treasure trove for jazz aficionados and anyone interested in Australia’s music history.

voyage.name: Box Hill Town Hall
voyage.content: An elegant example of 1930s civic architecture, Box Hill Town Hall now serves as a vibrant cultural and community centre.

voyage.name: Bulleen Art and Garden
voyage.content: A unique blend of garden centre and art space, it features local sculptures, pottery, and sustainable gardening products. A good spot for eco-conscious visitors and art enthusiasts.

voyage.name: Canterbury streetscapes
voyage.content: The charming, tree-lined residential streets of Canterbury are renowned for their elegant architecture and lush greenery. Best enjoyed on foot, these streetscapes showcase historic homes and manicured gardens, particularly around Wentworth and Hopetoun Avenues.

voyage.name: Hawthorn Town Hall
voyage.content: Built in 1890, this grand town hall showcases Second Empire-style architecture. It now functions as an arts and community hub with galleries and a performing arts centre.

voyage.name: Heide Museum of Modern Art
voyage.price: $16 adults, $14 seniors, $12 concessions, children (<12) and sculpture park entry free
voyage.content: Set on the Yarra River floodplains, Heide is internationally acclaimed for its collections of modern and contemporary art. Featuring three galleries and an outdoor sculpture garden, the museum is also renowned for its connection to iconic Australian artists such as Sidney Nolan.

voyage.name: Maling Road Village
voyage.content: Established in the 1800s, this quaint shopping village features boutique shops in heritage buildings. Known for its “old world” charm, Maling Road offers a delightful blend of cafes, antiques, and specialty stores.

voyage.name: Maranoa Botanic Gardens
voyage.hours: Mon-Fri 7:30AM-4PM, Sat Sun & public holidays noon-5PM, closed on Good Fri and Christmas Day
voyage.content: Established as one of Australia’s oldest native gardens, Maranoa Gardens offers a diverse range of over 4,000 native plants and peaceful pathways. Nestled next to Beckett Park, this is a serene retreat for nature lovers.

voyage.name: Melbourne Tram Museum
voyage.hours: 11AM-5PM, 2nd & 4th Sat each month (only 2nd Sat in December)
voyage.content: Housed in the historic Hawthorn Tram Depot, this museum holds 21 beautifully restored trams dating back to 1906, including the iconic W-class trams. Explore Melbourne’s tram history in a building with classic American Romanesque architecture.

voyage.name: Ramsay Street from Neighbours
voyage.content: Famous for being the filming location of the popular Australian TV show Neighbours. Fans can visit the street and recognize the classic homes from the show.

voyage.name: Ringwood Clocktower
voyage.content: War memorial with garden setting as well as a clock tower.

voyage.name: Schramm's Cottage
voyage.content: A well-preserved pioneer cottage and museum showcasing life in early Melbourne. It features historical displays, a blacksmith’s workshop, and gardens reflective of the 1800s.

voyage.name: Schwerkolt Cottage
voyage.content: This pioneer cottage, built in the 1880s, offers a fascinating look into early settler life. The well-preserved structure includes period furnishings and nearby interpretive displays that provide a glimpse into the history of Melbourne’s outer suburbs.

voyage.name: Box Hill Gardens
voyage.content: This tranquil park includes a lake, walking paths, and a beautiful Chinese pavilion. It’s popular for outdoor activities, picnics, and as a community gathering spot.

voyage.name: Blackburn Lake Sanctuary
voyage.content: A natural haven for wildlife and a peaceful retreat for visitors, this sanctuary offers trails, picnic areas, and a lake, all surrounded by lush bushland and native flora.

voyage.name: Jells Park
voyage.content: Featuring well-maintained paths and lovely picnic spots overlooking a lake, Jells Park is a popular destination for families and nature lovers alike.

voyage.name: Ringwood Lake Park
voyage.content: This family-friendly park includes a lake, walking trails, playgrounds, and picnic areas. It’s a popular spot for locals to relax and enjoy the outdoors.

voyage.name: Warrandyte State Park
voyage.content: Known for its natural beauty along the Yarra River, this park has scenic walking trails, picnic spots, and swimming areas. It’s ideal for those wanting a nature escape close to the city.

voyage.name: Wattle Park
voyage.content: Known for its 12,000 wattle trees, this large park offers golf, cricket, and walking paths. It’s a green slice of Australian bush nestled in suburban Melbourne.

voyage.name: Yarra Bend Park
voyage.content: 3 km from the CBD, Yarra Bend Park is a vast expanse of bushland and parkland along the Yarra River. Visitors can enjoy walking and cycling trails, boathouses, and picnic areas amidst natural beauty.

voyage.name: Koonung Creek Trail cycling and walking
voyage.content: A scenic and accessible trail, ideal for a leisurely cycle or walk through the eastern suburbs. Stretching from Kew to Nunawading, this trail passes through green parklands and bushland, with amenities such as toilets, drinking fountains, and shaded seating spots along the way. The path is sealed and well-signposted, making it suitable for all fitness levels.

voyage.name: Studley Park Boathouse paddling
voyage.price: Free entry; boat hire from $30 for two people for half-hour
voyage.content: Established in 1863, the Studley Park Boathouse offers a memorable paddling experience on the scenic Yarra River. Rent a rowboat, kayak, or canoe to explore the waterways, or enjoy walking tracks through the nearby parkland. There’s also a charming café and restaurant for refreshments after a day on the water.

voyage.name: Whitehorse Lunar New Year Festival
voyage.alt: Box Hill Chinese New Year Festival
voyage.content: Celebrate Melbourne’s multicultural spirit at this vibrant festival, one of the largest Chinese New Year events in the state. The festivities feature dragon and lion dances, traditional music, fireworks, and delicious street food. It’s an exciting way to experience Chinese culture, with activities and performances for the whole family. Free entry.

voyage.name: Warrandyte gold panning and bushwalking
voyage.price: Free, though a miner's right (permit) and personal equipment are required for gold panning
voyage.content: Step back in time and pan for gold along the Yarra River in Andersons Creek, just as prospectors did in the 1850s. Warrandyte State Park offers bushwalking trails and picnic spots with scenic river views, where you can try your luck at finding small flecks of gold.

voyage.name: Treetops Adventure Belgrave
voyage.content: Tackle your fear of heights at the Treetops Adventure Park. With courses ranging from beginner to advanced, this high-ropes adventure is perfect for thrill-seekers and nature lovers alike. The site features zip lines, rope bridges, and Tarzan swings suspended high in the eucalyptus trees, offering both excitement and gorgeous views.

voyage.name: Yarra River kayak tour
voyage.content: Experience Melbourne from a unique perspective with a self-guided kayak tour along the Yarra River. Paddle through peaceful stretches of natural bushland and keep an eye out for native wildlife, including kookaburras and water dragons.

voyage.name: Heide Museum of Modern Art sculpture garden tour
voyage.price: Free entry to garden; museum admission $16
voyage.content: Take an immersive outdoor tour through the Heide Museum’s sculpture garden, which houses over 30 works by Australia’s leading artists. The garden is an artistic escape that’s as much about nature as it is about sculpture, featuring pieces inspired by and integrated into the surrounding landscape.

voyage.name: Mullum Mullum Trail walking and biking
voyage.address: Runs through Mitcham, Ringwood, and Donvale, linking to Eastlink Trail.
voyage.content: A quieter alternative to some of the larger trails, Mullum Mullum Trail meanders through native bushland, passing wetlands, creeks, and local parks. This path is ideal for walkers and cyclists looking for a more secluded route with plenty of bird-watching opportunities.

voyage.name: SkyHigh Observatory and Gardens
voyage.content: Overlooking the Eastern suburbs, SkyHigh Mount Dandenong offers stunning views of Melbourne and its surroundings. The attraction features beautiful gardens, a maze, a bistro, and seasonal events. Perfect for a day trip, especially at sunset or twilight for picturesque views.

voyage.name: Box Hill Central Shopping Centre
voyage.content: Box Hill Central is a bustling shopping destination with a unique multicultural flair. Known for its diverse array of stores, it includes everything from popular fashion and electronics outlets to Asian grocery stores, herbal shops, and local produce markets. The extensive food court is a highlight, offering authentic Asian street food and snacks that reflect the cultural heart of the area. Perfect for daily shopping

voyage.name: Eastland Shopping Centre
voyage.content: Eastland is one of Melbourne’s premier shopping centres, blending popular fashion brands with boutique shops and a lively dining precinct. It features everything from high-end department stores like Myer to international retailers and a large Hoyts Cinema. Eastland’s open-air Town Square is also a top spot for dining, where visitors can enjoy a range of cuisines and relax after a shopping spree.

voyage.name: The Glen Shopping Centre
voyage.content: A popular retail hub, The Glen boasts an impressive selection of fashion, beauty, tech, and homeware retailers. Known for its stylish design, the centre includes a modern food court and a number of fine dining spots for a gourmet break during your visit. It’s an ideal shopping destination with plenty of variety and a relaxed atmosphere.

voyage.name: Glenferrie Road Hawthorn
voyage.content: Glenferrie Road is a lively, tree-lined shopping strip featuring stylish boutiques, bookstores, and local artisanal shops. This area is ideal for unique finds, from designer clothing and accessories to one-of-a-kind gifts and vintage treasures. Numerous cafes and eateries are scattered along the street, making it perfect for a leisurely day out.

voyage.name: Maling Road Village
voyage.content: With its charming Victorian streetscape, Maling Road Village is a must-visit for boutique shopping. The area is known for speciality stores selling handmade goods, antique shops, and galleries. It’s an excellent spot to find memorable souvenirs, including pottery, locally crafted jewellery, and unique artisan products. Quaint cafes and tea rooms add to the village’s inviting atmosphere.

voyage.name: Westfield Doncaster
voyage.content: Westfield Doncaster is one of Melbourne’s largest shopping centres, featuring an extensive range of Australian and international brands. From high-fashion stores and specialty boutiques to department stores and food options, it’s a one-stop shopping experience. The centre also includes a rooftop dining area with views of the city skyline—a perfect spot to unwind.

voyage.name: Westfield Knox
voyage.content: A popular shopping complex in the eastern suburbs, Westfield Knox is home to a wide selection of stores covering fashion, homewares, electronics, and more. The centre’s entertainment precinct includes a state-of-the-art cinema and an indoor play area for children, making it ideal for a full day of family shopping and leisure.

voyage.name: Camberwell Sunday Market
voyage.content: A beloved local market and an institution in Melbourne, the Camberwell Sunday Market is perfect for those searching for vintage treasures, antiques, artisan crafts, and unique souvenirs. With over 370 stalls, it’s a bustling spot where you can find everything from second-hand books and clothing to handcrafted jewelry and collectibles. Proceeds support local charities, making it a great place to shop for a cause.

voyage.name: Boroondara Farmers Market
voyage.content: An excellent spot for foodies, Boroondara Farmers Market showcases local, fresh produce, from seasonal fruits and vegetables to organic meats, artisanal cheeses, and gourmet condiments. It’s a great way to experience Victoria’s farm-to-table culture and pick up some unique, edible souvenirs. Vendors are friendly, often providing samples and sharing the stories behind their products.

voyage.name: Hooked Fish and Chipper Hawthorn
voyage.content: Fish&chips

voyage.name: Laksa Garden
voyage.content: Malaysian cuisine

voyage.name: Little Bad Wolf
voyage.content: An eclectic dining experience in a relaxed, modern setting. Known for its creative fusion dishes and inventive small plates, the menu caters to a variety of tastes, from gourmet burgers to Asian-inspired bites. Paired with a curated selection of craft beers and cocktails, it’s a spot for a casual meal or a lively night out.

voyage.name: Tien Dat
voyage.content: Tien Dat has been a longstanding favourite in Box Hill for authentic Vietnamese cuisine. Known for its warm atmosphere and attentive service, it offers a menu rich with traditional dishes like pho, banh xeo, and fresh rice paper rolls.

voyage.name: Box Hill Central Food Court
voyage.content: Bustling indoor food court boasting over 20 stalls serving a variety of budget-friendly East Asian meals, drinks and snacks including Chinese, Vietnamese and Malaysian.

voyage.name: Enoteca Boccaccio
voyage.content: A wine bar and Italian restaurant offering a selection of Italian-inspired dishes and an extensive wine list. It focuses on fresh, seasonal ingredients, pairing well with wines from Italy and Australia. The restaurant’s emphasis is on quality dining in a casual, welcoming setting.

voyage.name: Hunter & Barrel
voyage.content: Offering a premium dining experience, focusing on high-quality meats cooked over flames. The menu features steaks, burgers, and fresh dishes, complemented by a curated selection of wines, craft beers, and barrel-aged spirits.

voyage.name: Mister Bianco
voyage.content: Sicilian fine dining in an elegant atmosphere, showcasing Italian classics with a modern twist.

voyage.name: Olivigna
voyage.content: Nestled in a vineyard, olive grove and restaurant offering Mediterranean-inspired dishes crafted from local produce, including estate-grown olives and honey, handmade pasta, wood-fired pizzas, and house-cured meats.

voyage.name: The Peacock Den
voyage.content: A wine and dining venue in The Basin, The Peacock Den offers a relaxed setting for adults over 16, featuring premium wines, craft beers, and cocktails. Guests can enjoy share plates in a cosy atmosphere with plush couches and a fireplace, perfect for a laid-back evening with friends.

voyage.name: Prohibition Food & Wine
voyage.content: A relaxed dining venue in Burwood Village, offering a seasonally based menu designed for sharing. The venue features indoor and outdoor seating, including a beer garden. The restaurant serves a variety of dishes paired with a curated wine list, craft beers, and cocktails.

voyage.name: Bar Nearby
voyage.content: A welcoming space for a casual drink or an evening out. With a selection of cocktails, beers, and wines, it caters to a variety of tastes. The bar occasionally features live music and events, offering a relaxed setting to enjoy with friends or unwind after a busy day.

voyage.name: The Ten Saints
voyage.content: A lively bar and beer garden in Croydon, offering a wide selection of drinks including beer, cider, wine, and cocktails. Guests can enjoy the relaxed atmosphere and bring their own food, whether picking up a meal from local eateries or ordering in via Uber Eats.

voyage.name: The Kilburn
voyage.content: Cosy cocktail and wine bar in a former smoking lounge on the corner of Glenferrie and Burwood Roads.

voyage.name: Motel Maroondah
voyage.content: Basic budget rooms in roadside lodging with free Wi-Fi and parking close to Box Hill.

voyage.name: Sage Hotel
voyage.content: Modern accommodation with stylish rooms and convenient access to public transport and local attractions. The hotel features on-site dining, a fitness centre, and meeting facilities, making it suitable for both leisure and business stays. Spacious rooms with contemporary amenities, including free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Nightcap Shoppingtown Hotel
voyage.content: Offers comfortable 3½-star rooms and facilities centrally located to Doncaster Hill. The hotel also offers a bar and bistro, a nightclub and a cabaret room, hosting various performances and shows regularly throughout the year.

voyage.name: Warrandyte Goldfields Bed & Breakfast
voyage.content: A humble 4-star bed and breakfast in a scenic rural setting, right next to the main shopping strip of Warrandyte. Includes complimentary breakfast, Wi-Fi and Netflix.

voyage.name: The Sebel Melbourne Kew
voyage.content: Modern hotel located east of Kew Junction in a quiet residential area.

voyage.name: Brighton Beach and Bathing Boxes
voyage.content: One of Melbourne's favoured beaches, be sure to check out the infamous 'bathing boxes', brightly coloured boxes that are dotted along the sand.

voyage.name: Monash University Museum of Art
voyage.content: Monash University is one of the major tertiary institutions in Melbourne.

voyage.name: Rippon Lea Estate
voyage.content: A heritage-listed historic house and gardens.

voyage.name: Royal Botanic Gardens Cranbourne
voyage.address: Cnr Ballarto Road and Botanic Drive, Cranbourne

voyage.name: Drum Theatre
voyage.address: Corner Lonsdale and Walker streets, Dandenong
voyage.content: Opened in February 2006, Drum Theatre is a state-of-the-art, purpose built performing arts theatre within the heritage facade of the former Dandenong Town Hall, and situated in the heart of the Dandenong CBD.

voyage.name: Moonlit Sanctuary Wildlife Conservation Park
voyage.hours: 10AM-5PM (Night tours are available and must be booked in advance)
voyage.content: Eco-tourism zoo with rare and endangered Australia animals such as koala, kangaroo, wallaby, dingo, Tasmanian devil, wombat and birds. Koala petting is available at additional cost.

voyage.name: Australian National Aviation Museum
voyage.hours: Mon-Fri 10AM-4PM, Sat Sun 10AM-5PM, closed Good Fri, Christmas Day and Boxing Day
voyage.content: The Australian National Aviation Museum houses a substantial collection of over 50 civil and military aircraft, including several rare and locally significant types. Its exhibits chart the evolution of aviation in Australia from early pioneering designs through to the jet age, with many aircraft undergoing active restoration. Largely volunteer-run, the museum offers an informative and accessible insight into the coun

voyage.name: Lysterfield Park
voyage.content: Mountain Bike Trails including the State Mountain Bike course offers 20 kilometres of trails catering for riders of all ages and ability. The lake is very popular for canoeing, sailing, paddle boating and surf skiing. There are also a number of walking tracks including three trails that are linked for a brisk two-hour walk around the lake.

voyage.name: Caulfield Racecourse
voyage.content: Site of dozens of horse-racing events throughout the year.

voyage.name: Dandenong Market
voyage.hours: Open every Sun, Tue, Fri and Sat
voyage.content: Founded in 1866, Dandenong Market is Melbourne’s second oldest and second largest market. Products sold include fruit and veggies, bakeries, delis, seafood, butchers, honey, nuts, clothing, jewellery, flowers and books.

voyage.name: Chadstone Shopping Centre
voyage.content: The biggest shopping centre in the Southern Hemisphere. Two food courts, countless clothes shops (including a dedicated luxury fashion and accessories section), art, music, and daily essentials. Has express buses from the city and from Oakleigh Railway Station.

voyage.name: Westfield Southland Shopping Centre
voyage.content: Multi-storey shopping centre with two main sides, with a retail bridge that connects them over the Nepean Highway. Includes over four-hundred stores, two department stores, four discount department stores, and a sixteen screen Village Cinemas multiplex. Serviced by the adjacent Southland Station which is on the Frankston Line.

voyage.name: Ivan's Pies
voyage.content: Bakery.

voyage.name: Clayton Monash Motor Inn & Serviced Apartments
voyage.content: Inexpensive motel a short walk from Monash University and the Monash Medical Centre. Reasonable quality. On the major Princes Highway, so rooms near the front may be noisy.

voyage.name: Flinders Street Station
voyage.content: The defining landmark of Melbourne, this colonial-era railway station was designed in an 1899 competition. The station's front steps, below a row of clocks announcing train departure times, are a popular meeting point for locals. It is the busiest suburban station in the Southern Hemisphere. Although grand from the outside, the interior has become dilapidated over the years and many rooms including the ballroom are c

voyage.name: Government House
voyage.content: The official residence of the Governor of Victoria. The house opened in 1876 as the official residence of the Governor-General of Australia, before the capital moved to Canberra. The house is modelled to some extent on Queen Victoria's Osborne House, in Cowes, England. Combined tours with La Trobe's Cottage must be booked two weeks in advance. Free garden tours on third Thursday of the month, limited to 10 people so

voyage.name: Governor La Trobe's Cottage
voyage.hours: Oct - May on first and third Sundays 11AM - 4PM
voyage.address: Corner of Birdwood Avenue & Dallas Brooks Drive, The Domain
voyage.content: A prefabricated cottage imported from England in 1839 for Victoria's first Lt. Governor, Charles Joseph La Trobe. The cottage has been rebuilt and relocated. The cottage and garden is run by the National Trust.

voyage.name: Melbourne Town Hall
voyage.content: Built in 1870, the city's town hall is grand and historic. 1 hour tours allow visitors to see the ornate Council chambers, the richly-carved Grand Organ and sit in the Lord Mayor's chair. Bookings recommended.

voyage.name: Old Melbourne Gaol
voyage.price: $30 adult, $25 concession, $17 child (5-15yrs), family tickets available (free for National Trust members and members of reciprical trusts overseas)
voyage.hours: Daily 10AM-5PM except Good Fri and Christmas Day. Night tours: Mon, Wed, Fri and Sat
voyage.content: Built in 1841, it is now a penal museum, with a watch house and magistrate's court also on-site. Bushranger Ned Kelly was hanged here in 1880. The scaffold on which he and many others were hanged is displayed, as is Kelly’s death mask. There are other displays in many of the cells. Allow an hour or so for your visit.

voyage.name: Parliament House of Victoria
voyage.hours: Mon-Fri 9:30AM-3:45PM. Tours: Sat Sun 9:30AM, 10:30AM, 11:30AM, 1:30PM, 2:30PM and 3:45PM; on sitting Tuesdays, 9:30AM, 10:30AM and 11:30AM
voyage.content: Built between 1856 and 1879, the Australian federal parliament sat in this impressive building from 1901 to 1927 while Canberra was built. It now houses the state parliament. The majestic façade can be seen right down Bourke St. Tours of the assembly halls and libraries are conducted when parliament is not in session. Visitors are also welcome to sit in the public gallery when parliament is in session.

voyage.name: Scots Church
voyage.hours: Mon-Fri 11AM-2:30PM; Sun visits only for Mass services
voyage.content: Gothic church built in 1873, the first Presbyterian house of worship in the city.

voyage.name: Shrine of Remembrance
voyage.hours: daily 10AM - 5PM (last entry 4:30PM), closed Christmas Day and Good Fri
voyage.content: War memorial in classical style opened in 1934. The memorial was designed so that the sun would shine on the word LOVE at 11AM on 11 November. Exhibition galleries under the memorial were added in 2014. A Last Post Service is held here every Sunday at 4.45pm to commemorate an important event in Australia's military history.

voyage.name: State Library of Victoria
voyage.content: Built in stages beginning in 1854, it has an impressive classical revival façade. Includes a good newspaper reading room, genealogy room and an art collection, as well as the fantastic La Trobe Reading Room and its huge dome. Bushranger Ned Kelly's armour is stored permanently on display, along with a variety of galleries and exhibitions. Internet terminals are provided for research only, not email, and usually need

voyage.name: St Michaels Uniting Church
voyage.content: Romanesque-style church built in 1866.

voyage.name: St Patrick’s Cathedral
voyage.content: The original part of this Gothic Revival cathedral was built in the 1850s. It was consecrated in 1897 and the spires added in 1939. It is the largest and tallest church in Australia.

voyage.name: St Paul's Cathedral
voyage.content: Gothic-revival cathedral on the site of the colony's first church services in 1836.

voyage.name: Crown Entertainment Complex
voyage.hours: 24hr daily, closed 4AM-noon Christmas Day, Good Fri, and Anzac Day.
voyage.content: A Las Vegas-style gambling palace (including the Crown Casino), also containing restaurants, upmarket boutiques, nightclubs, two hotel towers, a cinema complex and floorshows.

voyage.name: Eureka Tower
voyage.price: $18.50 adult, $14 concession, $10 child (4-16yrs) and various family tickets. Discounted price for additional same-day visit at nighttime
voyage.content: Contains the highest observation deck in the Southern Hemisphere on level 88, with panoramic views of the entirety of Melbourne. Only recommended in clear weather. Also offers an additional cost "Edge" experience whereby visitors are protruded outside of the building inside a glass-panelled cube.

voyage.name: Federation Square
voyage.content: The city's most popular meeting place. The striking architecture of its buildings create a nice backdrop to this open plaza, directly opposite Flinders Street Station. There are usually live, free performances from various groups, along with coverage of major sporting and cultural events on the huge television. A number of museums and organisations call the site home, as well as Melbourne's major visitor information

voyage.name: Melbourne Aquarium
voyage.price: $35 adult, $21.50 child (4-15 yr), $29 concession, $92 family (2 adult+2 children); discounts online
voyage.address: Cnr Flinders St and Kings Way
voyage.content: Home to over 10,000 aquatic creatures, there are four distinct areas of the aquarium dedicated to Antarctica, seahorses, the rainforest and the ocean, the latter of which includes a glass walk-through experience. Shark diving and animal feeding available.

voyage.name: ACDC Lane
voyage.content: Formerly Corporation Lane, this alley was renamed in 2004 in honour of the world-famous Australian rock band. The laneway's sign is a nice photo opportunity for fans, plus it's located in the bar and rock district of the city.

voyage.name: Hosier Lane
voyage.content: If you want to sample street art, head for this little lane full of ever-evolving, colourful graffiti from end to end.

voyage.name: Australian Centre for the Moving Image
voyage.price: General entry free; charges apply for exhibitions
voyage.content: A museum, gallery and collection of cinemas dedicated to film, TV, video games, new media and art, both old and new. Regularly holds a number of interesting exhibitions.

voyage.name: The Ian Potter Centre
voyage.hours: Tue-Sun 10AM-5PM, except Christmas Day and Good Fri; 1PM on ANZAC Day
voyage.content: Houses over 25,000 works of only Australian art, including paintings, sculptures, photography and fashion. Famous artists such as Frederick McCubbin and Sidney Nolan are on display, along with a fine collection of Indigenous art.

voyage.name: National Gallery of Victoria
voyage.hours: Wed-Mon 10AM-5PM, except Christmas Day and Good Fri; 1PM on ANZAC Day
voyage.content: The premier venue for international fine art exhibitions in Melbourne, with a permanent collection and international collections. A must-see for art lovers.

voyage.name: Arts Centre Melbourne
voyage.content: The Arts Centre Melbourne is home to the Melbourne Symphony Orchestra, the Australian Ballet, Opera Australia and the Melbourne Theatre Company. It has a variety of performance venues, exhibition spaces, bars and restaurants. On Sundays, it hosts an Artisans' Market.

voyage.name: Koorie Heritage Trust
voyage.content: Showcases contemporary art from Victorian First Peoples.

voyage.name: ANZ Banking Museum
voyage.content: Housed in the late-19th century Gothic Revival ANZ Bank building, it walks through the history of Australian banking from Indigenous bartering economies to finance of the future.

voyage.name: Chinese Museum
voyage.hours: Daily 10AM-5PM, closed Good Fri, Christmas and New Year's Day
voyage.content: Situated in the midst of Chinatown, it documents and explains the history of Chinese immigrants in Australia. The 'millennium dragon' is on display, the largest Chinese dragon in the world, along with an interactive underground exhibit highlighting the goldfields. Also on-site is a free visitor centre and a gift shop. The museum runs walking tours of Chinatown by appointment ($10 per person).

voyage.name: Fire Services Museum
voyage.content: A largely niche museum, it is the largest fire service-related collection in Australia. Houses historical uniforms, vehicles, photos and other memorabilia.

voyage.name: Immigration Museum
voyage.hours: Daily 10AM-5PM except Good Fri & Christmas Day
voyage.content: Located in the restored Old Customs House, it covers customs and immigration history over the past 200 years. Details the stories and experiences of immigrations to Australia, both past and present.

voyage.name: Old Treasury Building and Gold Museum
voyage.hours: Sun-Fri 10AM-4PM, closed Good Fri, Christmas and Boxing Day
voyage.content: Built in 1858 by a 19-year-old architect, it was the city’s first Italian Renaissance building and many consider that its elegance has not been surpassed by anything in Melbourne since. Contains displays on the history of Melbourne as well as the history of gold in Victoria, including the original gold vaults. Fun activities for children, including the chance to earn a novelty gold licence. The expansive Treasury Gar

voyage.name: Polly Woodside Maritime Museum
voyage.hours: Daily in Summer, July school holidays and weekends in Winter: 10AM-4PM
voyage.content: A maritime museum based aboard the restored 1885 Belfast-built, three-masted, iron-hulled barque "Polly Woodside". Various kids activities available, including Pirate Sundays.

voyage.name: Victoria Police Museum
voyage.content: Displays with over 150 years of stories and of crime, justice, courage and forensic techniques. Includes some of the famous Kelly Gang's armour, the burnt out car used in the Russell Street Police HQ bombing and various records about famous gangland figures. Regular free exhibitions are on display.

voyage.name: Alexandra Gardens
voyage.content: Ornamental gardens laid out in 1904, on south bank of the Yarra River. There is a row of historic rowing boathouses on the river bank.

voyage.name: Cooks' Cottage and Fitzroy Gardens
voyage.hours: Cooks' Cottage: Daily 10AM-4PM, closed Christmas Day
voyage.content: Cooks' Cottage is the cottage that belonged to Captain James Cook’s parents and was transported from Yorkshire to Melbourne in 1934.

voyage.name: Queen Victoria Gardens
voyage.content: Features memorials to Queen Victoria and King Edward VII, sculptures and a floral clock of 7000 plants.

voyage.name: Royal Botanic Gardens
voyage.content: Recognised as one of the world’s finest botanic gardens, with over 10,000 species and 50,000 individual plants in the 38 hectare gardens.

voyage.name: O'Brien Icehouse
voyage.content: The largest ice recreation venue in the Southern Hemisphere, the O'Brien Icehouse allows visitors to skate around a large ice rink. There are free beginner classes on weekends and school holidays. It regularly holds public events such as dancing, games, and music parties.

voyage.name: Bourke Street Mall
voyage.content: A popular pedestrian and tram-only mall in the CBD lined with both big-name fashion brands and start-up designers.

voyage.name: Fat
voyage.content: Renowned for discovering some of Australia's most beloved labels; stocks emerging labels as well as the now established brands.

voyage.name: David Jones
voyage.content: Large, multi-level store of the higher-end department store chain.

voyage.name: H&M
voyage.content: Famous Swedish retailer's first store in Australia, housed in the historic General Post Office building. Sells a variety of cheap, quality womens, mens and kids clothing, along with a variety of home furnishings.

voyage.name: Myer
voyage.content: The renovated, flagship store of Australia's largest department store chain.

voyage.name: Aesop
voyage.content: A Melbourne-born brand started in 1987, Aesop is decked out in apothecary style and uses botanical extracts and natural preservatives where possible. Their products will definitely earn a prized rank in your bathroom.

voyage.name: City Hatters
voyage.content: A famous icon for many Melbournians, the City Hatters sits just beneath the main entrance to Flinders Street Station on the right. It has survived the test of time, opening at the location in 1910, and stocks a wide variety of accessories, mostly for men. The store also provides hat cleaning and measurement services.

voyage.name: Block Arcade
voyage.address: 280 Collins St through to Elizabeth St
voyage.content: A historic shopping arcade built in 1891, lined with boutiques and cafés, housed within carved stone and wood walls with a glass canopy above.

voyage.name: Royal Arcade
voyage.content: Built in 1870, it is a historic shopping arcade that runs between Little Collins St, the Bourke Street Mall and Elizabeth St. The carved statues standing guard next to the iconic clock are worth a look, along with the numerous small shops.

voyage.name: Emporium Melbourne
voyage.content: Opened in 2014, it is housed within the former Myer Emporium building. The centre has cemented itself in the high-end shopping scene, home to major international fashion brands in addition to flagship Japanese retailer Uniqlo.

voyage.name: Harbour Town
voyage.content: An open-air shopping centre of factory outlet stores with a number of major brands. Prides itself on big bargains and discounts, although the prices are nothing spectacular.

voyage.name: Melbourne Central
voyage.content: It used to be the only shopping centre in the CBD, but now has a lot of competition. Sits above the train station of the same name, and home to a large variety of stores and brands. An old shot tower sits within the centre's iconic glass cone roof, along with a small museum display about the tower's history and a clock (The Marionette Watch) which plays Waltzing Matilda every hour.

voyage.name: QV Melbourne
voyage.content: Multi-storey shopping centre next to the State Library and opposite Melbourne Central, with a number of large supermarket and department stores such as Big W, Woolworths, Harvey Norman and Domayne Furniture.

voyage.name: Queen Victoria Market
voyage.content: The largest open air market in the Southern Hemisphere, officially opened in 1878. The market has a mixture of outdoor stalls and indoor halls, selling food, clothes and crafts.

voyage.name: The Melbourne Shop by Lumbi
voyage.content: A variety of high-quality wares such as mugs, cushions, phone cases, clocks and a Melbourne-style Snakes and Ladders rip-off. Items are assembled in Yarraville in the city's west.

voyage.name: Outre Gallery
voyage.content: For the art lover that doesn't have a lot to spend, Outre can get you started with originals for under $100.

voyage.name: Arts Centre's Sunday Market
voyage.address: Between Hamer Hall and Arts Centre Melbourne
voyage.content: Every Sunday, the small park between Hamer Hall and Arts Centre Melbourne is filled with stalls that sell arts and crafts locally made by the sellers. The place is animated with live performance at noon.

voyage.name: Aix
voyage.content: Has a huge selection of mouth-wateringly good crepes.

voyage.name: Manchester Press
voyage.content: Specialty coffee, brekkie and bagels served in a light, vintage-chic cafe with eclectic decor.

voyage.name: Axil
voyage.content: Shop with barista who won 'Best Barista in the World' award in 2022, serving coffee, brekkie and light meals. Multiple locations across the CBD and Melbourne.

voyage.name: Brunetti Oro Melbourne City
voyage.content: Beautiful Italian cakes, desserts, and coffee. Available until late at night.

voyage.name: Royal Stacks
voyage.content: Royal Stacks is a mini homage to US burger chain, Shake Shack

voyage.name: Simpsons Burgers
voyage.content: Small shop serving a wide variety of burgers and sides, including chips and salads. Includes vegetarian options.

voyage.name: Camy Shanghai Dumplings
voyage.content: Chinese food in large servings, notable for its dumplings. Meals served with complimentary tea.

voyage.name: Shanghai Street
voyage.content: Cheap and cheerful dumplings, expect a queue as they don't take bookings

voyage.name: Gaylords
voyage.content: Kitschy ode to Bollywood in the heart of Chinatown.

voyage.name: Tonka
voyage.content: A ritzy, reservations-required Indian/Modern Australian fusion restaurant down one of Melbourne's most iconic laneways.

voyage.name: Crossways
voyage.content: Tasty lunch cafe with a 2-course vegetarian all-you-can-eat meal. May be possible to work 30 minutes for your meal.

voyage.name: Gopals Pure Vegetarian
voyage.content: Sister restaurant to Crossways.

voyage.name: Om Vegetarian
voyage.content: Cheap vegetarian and vegan buffet-style food which changes every day.

voyage.name: Stalactites
voyage.content: This Greek restaurant decorated with stalactites has delicious gyros and earthy meals.

voyage.name: Hella Good
voyage.content: Classic souvlaki place with two locations in the heart of Melbourne (the listed and another at Emporium Melbourne); open until midnight for late-night feasts.

voyage.name: Il Mercato Centrale
voyage.content: A recreation of food markets in Italy, this covered area features over 20 shops selling everything from gelato to panini.

voyage.name: Brunetti Oro Flinders Lane
voyage.content: A large Italian café, bar and restaurant serving a range of sweet and savoury food and drinks with lots of indoor and outdoor seating. One of two Brunetti Oro cafes in the city, the other being on Little Collins Street at Swanston Street.

voyage.name: Romanello
voyage.content: A small shop selling pizzas by the slice and freshly-made porchetta rolls next to the Queen Victoria Market.

voyage.name: Cecconi's
voyage.content: A long-standing stalwart of Melbourne's food scene, this is a fine dining restaurant featuring modern takes on Italian cuisine.

voyage.name: Mama’s Bưởi
voyage.content: Set in the modernised historic building of the Melbourne General Post Office, this Vietnamese restaurant offers quality meals at reasonable prices. As an indication, a set menu meal costs $25 each and includes a drink, entree and main, with four choices in each.

voyage.name: Rozzis State Library
voyage.content: A small cornerside New York-style pizza place. Prices tend to be a little on the higher end ($5–7/slice) but the slices are reasonably large and filling.

voyage.name: Degraves Espresso Bar
voyage.content: Tucked into a bluestone laneway near Flinders St Station, this outlet has long-held the title of Melbourne's best coffee. Hours: M–F 6:30AM–7:30PM, Sa Su 7:30AM-6:30PM.

voyage.name: Brother Baba Budan
voyage.content: Speciality coffee shop serving cakes in a quirky space with wood panelling and bar stools.

voyage.name: Patricia Coffee Brewers
voyage.address: Little Bourke St & Little William St
voyage.content: Trendy, bare-bones, standing-room-only spot for artisanal coffee ground on-site, and small treats.

voyage.name: Dukes Coffee Roasters
voyage.content: Speciality outpost crafting home-grown coffee in a stylish interior with light, wood-panelled walls.

voyage.name: Naked Espresso Bar
voyage.content: They claim to specialise in serving and educating their customers all about speciality coffee. Their premium house blend, “Mega Choc” is always on offer, along with a rotating single origin of the day. Also on order are alternative brewing methods such as Aeropress, V60, Syphon and Cold Drip.

voyage.name: 65 Degrees
voyage.content: The owners have a long history of accolades. Champion barista, world latte artist and award winning coffee blend, gridlock coffee. Fast, friendly service and some of the finest coffee around.

voyage.name: The Gin Palace
voyage.content: Serious cocktail aficionados should check out this place, for a welcome mix of knowledgeable bartenders, funky bordello ambiance and a laid-back crowd.

voyage.name: The Carlton Club
voyage.content: Melbourne. Great late night joint or middle of the day, very functional with heaps of little spaces to get cosy and open areas to get your Sunday on. The rooftop bar in up there with the best in town. A must for people coming to Melbourne.

voyage.name: The Croft Institute
voyage.content: It epitomizes the kitschy-hidden-bar trend of the past few years. Tucked within the narrowest and smelliest alley in Melbourne, this place is somewhat charmingly fitted out like a high school laboratory; complete with beakers, test tubes and retorts. Check out the upstairs 'gymnasium' playing house and electro, and the hospital gurney (with stirrups) on display near the women's toilets.

voyage.name: Cookie
voyage.content: Excellent bar and cocktails with an upstyle crowd that likes to party hard. Has a restaurant upstairs for dinner serving excellent Thai-inspired meals.

voyage.name: Section 8
voyage.content: A bar in a car park made from shipping containers. 'Nuff said?

voyage.name: Madame Brussels
voyage.content: This English Garden party themed bar is on the roof and serves up excellent cocktails by staff in Tennis outfits. Cocktail jugs $30 and $50, 2+ and 4+ serves respectively

voyage.name: The Workshop Bar
voyage.content: This relaxed bar is in a former motorcycle workshop, hence the name. Run by the same people who run e55.

voyage.name: Heartbreaker
voyage.content: Bar with an extensive beer list and a solid decor. Also specialises in pizza and with a friendly staff.

voyage.name: CityTempo Apartments
voyage.content: compact CBD apartments on Queen Street near the Queen Vic Markets. 4 Stars (AAA Tourism), all linen/towels provided with kitchenettes. Some apartments include clothes washer/dryer.

voyage.name: Flinders Backpackers
voyage.price: 4-bed dorm bed $27/night or $160/week, twin/double $672/night or $439/week, double ensuite $84/night or $499/week
voyage.content: 24-hour reception. Centrally located. Twins and doubles have TV. A party hostel, with a nightclub just below the rooms, which will be noisy well into the night. Has many long-term residents, some of who may be unkind to tourists on vacation schedules.

voyage.name: Melbourne Central YHA
voyage.price: Shared room from $33.50, Double $78.50 (YHA members get $3.50 discount)
voyage.content: Centrally-located hostel in the backpacker hub of Melbourne. It is situated along the City Circle tram route and most Melbourne attractions are within walking distance. The staff are friendly, helpful and caring. It was opened in 2009 and is highly maintained.

voyage.name: Nomads Melbourne
voyage.price: Shared dorm from $19, double room from $70
voyage.content: Directly opposite the Queen Victoria Market.

voyage.name: Roamer Melbourne
voyage.content: Opposite Flinders Street Station, in the centre of Melbourne.Dormitory beds and ensuite private rooms.

voyage.name: Atlantis Hotel
voyage.content: 24 hour reception

voyage.name: Best Western Melbourne City Hotel
voyage.content: 24 hour reception.

voyage.name: Rydges Melbourne
voyage.content: 360 bedroom hotel with Locanda bar and restaurant (mains $27 - 59).

voyage.name: Citadines on Bourke Melbourne
voyage.content: Apartments available range from studios to two-bedroom executives, and have separate living and dining areas. It also offers a flexible service menu.

voyage.name: Rendezvous Hotel Melbourne
voyage.content: One of Australia’s finest historic hotels. Built in 1913, this meticulously restored hotel retains the elegant style of the early 1900s while providing you with all the convenience of 21st century technology and amenities. Parking available.

voyage.name: The Westin Melbourne
voyage.content: Modern, chic and elegantly understated.

voyage.name: Park Hyatt
voyage.content: Superior service. With Italian marble bathrooms complete with a deep sunken bath with inset TV, twin basins, separate lavatory and therapeutic shower.

voyage.name: Grand Hotel Melbourne
voyage.content: This heritage-listed apartment hotel has been restored to retain the style of the 1880s while providing guests with modern facilities.

voyage.name: Grand Hyatt Melbourne
voyage.content: Art Deco style hotel with Veronese marble and international art. All rooms receive access to the Regency Health Club, open daily from 6AM.

voyage.name: Hotel Windsor
voyage.content: The grand old lady of Melbourne's five-star hotels, and the only surviving grand pre-World War II hotel in Australia. Built in 1883, the Hotel Windsor bills itself as Australia’s only remaining grand hotel. It possesses old world charm with modern luxuries and is opposite Parliament at the top end of Collins St.

voyage.name: The Langham Melbourne Hotel
voyage.content: The Langham Melbourne hotel offers luxurious Melbourne city accommodation behind the high end Southgate shopping mall, opposite the historic Flinders Street Station. The Langham Melbourne Hotel was the only Australian hotel in Travel and Leisure magazine's list of the world's 100 best hotels (2009). The Langham's Chuan Spa also achieved 'Top Hotel Spa' status in Travel + Leisure USA's 2009 World’s Best Awards readers

voyage.name: Clarion Suites Gateway
voyage.content: Melbourne CBD hotel which is overlooking the Yarra River and is in the heart of Melbourne’s central business district. All suite and 4,5 stars Melbourne CBD hotel.

voyage.name: Quay West Suites Melbourne
voyage.content: This Southbank hotel is ideally positioned among Southbank promenade and overlooks the picturesque Yarra River.

voyage.name: Treasury on Collins Apartment Hotel
voyage.content: On the corner of Queens Street and Collins Street in the heart of Melbourne’s business district. Elegantly restored. this 19th century former bank is now an historic hotel.

voyage.name: Jewish Museum of Australia
voyage.content: An engaging museum that depicts the story of the Jewish community in Melbourne and Australia, in addition to the history of the strong local congregation within St Kilda and Caulfield. Houses a number of artefacts from around the world. Guided tours available on request.

voyage.name: St Kilda Beach
voyage.content: One of Melbourne's most famous and popular beaches, it is an enjoyable place to spend an afternoon. Apart from the omnipresent swimming, popular activities include sunbathing, sailing, beach volleyball, sandcastle-building, jetskiing and kitesurfing. The beach is regularly patrolled in the Summer by surf lifesavers.

voyage.name: St Kilda Botanical Gardens
voyage.hours: Gardens: sunrise–sunset, conservatory: Mon–Fri 10:30AM–3:30PM, Sat Sun sunrise–sunset
voyage.content: St Kilda's own botanical gardens were established in the 1800s and are an oasis of tranquility amongst the area's bustling surrounds. A short five minute walk down a side street from St Kilda's main hub, its features include a large conservatory, glasshouses, a gazebo, playground, a giant chess board and an ornamental lake. Detailed information about the plants and wildlife are available on the council's website.

voyage.name: St Kilda Pier, Breakwater and Kiosk
voyage.alt: Home of St Kilda's Little Penguin colony
voyage.content: The long, wooden pier is a popular spot for walking and fishing. Many of the fishermen along the pier will be happy to show you their catch if politely asked. At the end of the pier sits the historic kiosk, now a restaurant, which was rebuilt to the original plans in 2006 after an earlier arson attack. At the far end of the pier is the St Kilda breakwater, which is home to native water rats and the popular little pen

voyage.name: Victorian Pride Centre
voyage.content: Modern building that provides meeting spaces for LGBTQIA+ groups and communities as well as activism.

voyage.name: Palais Theatre
voyage.content: 1920s theatre that frequently hosts live music, comedy and ballet acts.

voyage.name: Luna Park
voyage.price: Single ride: adult (13+) $11, child (4-12) $9, infant $5; unlimited ticket: adult $49.50, child $39.50, infant $16.50
voyage.hours: Opening hours vary, although generally open 11AM-6PM weekends and 11AM-8PM weekdays during school holidays; closed weekdays during school term
voyage.content: This St Kilda icon's famous mouth entrance continues to grace Melbourne's postcards and for good reason. Built in 1912, the historic amusement park is free to enter, with a number of rides to keep the young and young at heart entertained. The fabled Scenic Railway is the oldest continually operating wooden-framed rollercoaster in the world, and gives panoramic views over the nearby bay. Other rides include all the us

voyage.name: St Kilda Sea Baths
voyage.content: An old Melbourne institution perched on the St Kilda foreshore, the Sea Baths building now has a variety of different functions, including a gymnasium, a spa, a sea water pool and countless restaurants, bars and cafés.

voyage.name: The Solar System Walk
voyage.content: A walk that has an exact scale model of the solar system, from size to distance, including Alpha Centauri, the closest star we can see with our naked eyes.

voyage.name: Acland Street Plaza
voyage.content: The cultural hub of St. Kilda. Pedestrianized Plaza bustling with eclectic shops, cafes, and street performers.

voyage.name: La Roche
voyage.content: La Roche in Acland Street has $5 pizzas and $6 pastas on some nights as well as cheap drinks. Favoured by younger locals and students.

voyage.name: Bala's
voyage.content: Opposite Luna Park, for the budget traveller.

voyage.name: Rococo
voyage.content: Excellent quality food. Pizza and pasta. Sit inside near the fire in winter or on Acland St.

voyage.name: Donovans
voyage.content: Opposite the beach and evening sunsets. An Age 2-Hat restaurant. Superb food at a pricey cost.

voyage.name: Stokehouse
voyage.content: Almost next door to Donovans. An Age 1-Hat restaurant. Posh place for chilling and excellent food.

voyage.name: Café di Stasio
voyage.content: Superb elegant Italian food.

voyage.name: Prince Bandroom
voyage.content: Many big local and international bands and DJs play here when in Melbourne.

voyage.name: Hotel Esplanade
voyage.content: Open since 1878, for over 100 years the Esplanade Hotel has been one of Melbourne's and indeed Australia's premier live music venues. Since the early days of string performances in the late 1800s the Espy's hallowed stages have been graced by many of Australia's and the world's major musicians, as well as other acts such as stand-up comedians. On an average week the pub plays host to over 50 bands across 3 stages, mu

voyage.name: The Ritz Backpackers
voyage.content: Renovated in 2025. Above the Elephant and Wheelbarrow hotel. Free breakfast daily and a great place to stay. You can park in the carpark behind the hotel overnight till 8AM, but you will probably get away with parking there a bit longer.

voyage.name: Nomads
voyage.price: $120pn for single room/ $40-$60 for dorm bed
voyage.content: Very clean and tidy hostel with plenty of communal space. New building (2024)

voyage.name: Roamer St Kilda
voyage.content: Friendly staff. Magnificent old building built in 1871. One of Melbourne's largest and most popular backpackers with 4-,6-, 8-, and 10-bed dorms, some en suite. Free pancake breakfast, large kitchen/communal lounge area and social events every night.

voyage.name: St Kilda Central Apartments
voyage.content: This property consists of self-contained units each owned by individual investors. They are very neat and tidy if a little unexciting. No street noise. Reasonable value if you have a car as you can park for free in the Aldi car park which is down stairs. Book through internet booking sites

voyage.name: Novotel St Kilda
voyage.content: The high-end of St Kilda's hotels offers a heated pool, gym, 24-hour room service and rooms with a breathtaking view over the water. A number of different room configurations available, from a queen double to a high-class penthouse with one or two bedrooms.

voyage.name: Albert Park and Lake
voyage.content: Public parkland and lake

voyage.name: Montague Street Bridge
voyage.content: One of Melbourne's lowest bridges at only 3.0 metres, leading to the result of constant crashes on the bridge and became the site of urban Melbourne legend. A website exists to measure days since there was last a crash on the Montague St Bridge and as of August 25, the median sits at a good 26 days.

voyage.name: Princes Pier
voyage.content: A small waterfront pier with many old wooden structures. It's a popular spot with photographers as not only does it provide a nice backdrop, but also makes for a nice sunset view.

voyage.name: Station Pier
voyage.content: One of the larger piers with a more extensive view of Port Melbourne. Parking is also readily available, as is public transport access.

voyage.name: South Melbourne Market
voyage.content: A large food and retail market, with lots of shops selling fresh food as well as delis, cafes and clothes shops. It retains many of the features of yesteryear.

voyage.name: Woolworths South Melbourne
voyage.content: Supermarket opposite the market.

voyage.name: Grays
voyage.content: An eclectic mix of 20th-century decorative and household items. Stock can include some relatively inexpensive home furnishings. Stuff seems to change regularly.

voyage.name: Avenue Bookstore
voyage.content: This excellent bookstore has a wide range of well selected works.

voyage.name: Andrew's Hamburgers
voyage.content: Popular old-school hamburger cafe

voyage.name: Brumby's Albert Park
voyage.content: Budget bakery and cafe.

voyage.name: Misuzu's
voyage.content: Upper mid-range to splurge Japanese food.

voyage.name: Third Wave BBQ Albert Park
voyage.content: American BBQ restaurant.

voyage.name: The Pullman Hotel Albert Park
voyage.content: Ideally located opposite Albert Park Lake, home of Australia’s Grand Prix track. A modern Albert Park hotel moments from St Kilda Road business district and a short tram ride to Melbourne's CBD.

voyage.name: Napier Cottage
voyage.content: A lovely 2 bedroom cottage situated only 5 minutes walk from the Clarendon Street shopping precinct.

voyage.name: The Blackman – An Art Series Hotel
voyage.content: A five-star boutique with 207 rooms. The hotel was named for artist Charles Blackman and was built immediately behind the historic Airlie Mansion.
